name: keyboard
title: Interactive Keyboard
description: A light 75% keyboard drawn as tiny square keys, from the function row down to the arrow cluster. Clicking a key, or typing on the real keyboard while it is in view, squeezes that key.
use: A page teaches keyboard shortcuts and needs a recognisable keyboard that reacts to real presses.
avoid: It is a display, not a text field; on phones the tiny keys are hard to read and tap.
a11y: Real key presses are caught, but tabbing to a key and pressing Enter does not fire it; icon-only keys lack labels. (keyboard: partial, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A pale grey keyboard about 900px wide on a black stage, wrapped in a rounded shell. Five rows of small keys carry tiny labels, with a wide space bar and a compact arrow cluster at the lower right.
behaves: Each key dips slightly on press, from a mouse click or from a real key press while the board is on screen. An optional line above can echo the last key, and optional per-key sounds play if enabled.
customise: Only className, enableSound and showPreview are exposed. Key layout, labels and colours are fixed in the source, so changing the board means editing the file.
weight: moderate: About eighty key buttons plus an intersection observer and an optional audio sprite.
